reflection_text.11:
The form is head-final on the day material and the split in round 1 is now between the colour-adjacent next-day reading and the Russian-language day-measure reading.

Background I keep from round 0–1: the lujvo can be read as a left-branching tanru ((rusy bavlam) dei) with dei ~ djedi ‘day’ as head. With that head the classic next-day place frame is d1 = the day in question, d2 = the day that is next to / precedes / follows d1 in the balvi/lamji relation, d3 = the day standard/calendar. The left modifier is then mapped onto d1. If rusy- is taken as the rusku ‘gray/grey’ rafsi and bavlam- as the balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’ material, the modifier only colours d1 and the free places stay

r1 = d1 = a rusy-coloured / bavlam-modified day
r2 = d2 = the day that stands next to / precedes r1
r3 = d3 = the day standard

i.e. the G description, essentially the A/D adjacency reading made explicit in the day place structure: x2 is the day preceding/adjacent to x1 and x3 is the day standard. The suppressed r4 = c2 place of the bavlam modifier is merged in the normal tanru mapping.

Round 1 public pressure is now moving toward the measure reading E. The E bloc argues morphologically:

* rusy is the fu’ivla for Russian, not a valid rafsi of rusku ‘gray’. The colour rafsi would be rus-, rusku-, not rusy-.
* bavla is ‘language/speech’; balvi ‘be next to’ is not bavla. The segmentation that fits the rafsi inventory is rusy-bavla-m-dei = [rusy bavla] ‘Russian language’ modifying mdei ~ djedi ‘day’.
* With rusy bavla as a modifier of a mdei head the head keeps its day-count/measure place structure: x1 is the interval/item being dated/measured, x2 is the quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1, x3 is the day standard/calendar against which the count is made. rusy bavla only narrows what kind of x1 we are talking about; it does not create new colour or adjacency places.

That gives x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1 and x3 = ‘day standard’, the E reading. The same standard x3 is shared with the G reading, the difference being x2 = preceding/adjacent day vs x2 = numerical day count.

The G bloc persists with:

* rusy- = rusku ‘gray’ colour/metaphorical modifier of the head;
* bavlamdei = the attested next-day/adjacent-day lujvo balvi + djedi;
* tanru place inheritance maps rusy bavlam onto d1 of djedi, leaving d2/d3 free as predecessor day and day standard.

A/D formulations are the same adjacency relation expressed without making the day head explicit, i.e. x2 adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, with D making x3 a property/sequence. Those are essentially the bavlam component re-analysed with a medju/lamji head rather than a djedi head.

Unresolved and still matters for final choice:

* Whether rusy can legitimately be read as a colour rafsi of rusku versus being the fu’ivla ‘Russian’. The rafsi inventory favours rus- for rusku and rusy for the language fu’ivla.
* Whether bavlam- is balvi/lamji adjacency material or bavla ‘language’ + linking m- before mdei. The transparent segmentation rusy bavla m dei is morphologically cleaner than rusy bav lam dei.
* Place-structure stability: the day head is stable under either reading; the difference is only the colouring of x1 and the interpretation of x2, which shifts from a predecessor day in the G next-day frame to a numerical day count in the E measure frame.

Current best estimate after integrating round 1: the morphological constraints most naturally support rusy = Russian fu’ivla and bavla = language, giving the day-measure lujvo with x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1 and x3 = day standard, i.e. E. The G gray-adjacent next-day reading remains a coherent alternative if rusy is allowed as a colour rafsi and bavlamdei is taken as the established adjacent-day compound, and it is the reading on which the earlier A/D adjacency statements are based.
reflection_text.15:
The term is being read as a head-final tanru/lujvo with the rightmost head mdei/dei ~ djedi ‘day’. The entire debate is about the left material and how it maps onto the head’s places.

* rusy-. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 continue to treat rusy- as the colour rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’ and therefore colour x1 only. Colleagues 10,13,14,16,17,2,21,5,7,9 now argue the more standard lexical fact is rusy- = the fu’ivla rafsi for rusko ‘Russian’, and bavla = ‘language/speech’. On that reading rusy bavla is the regular tanru ‘Russian language’ which qualifies x1, and rusy is not a colour modifier at all. The colour reading forces rusy = gray and bavlam = balvi/lamji adjacency.

* bavlam-/bavla-. The G bloc parses the form as rusy- bavlam-dei, i.e. rusy modifying the pre-existing next-day/adjacent-day lujvo bavlamdei ≃ balvi ‘be next to/be beside’ + djedi ‘day’. With the head djedi the classic next-day place frame is inherited:
x1 = the day in question,
x2 = the day that x1 is next to / precedes/follows,
x3 = the day standard/calendar.
With rusy as colour modifier the modifier saturates x1, so r1 = gray day, r2 = the day adjacent/preceding r1, r3 = day standard. That is the G description, essentially the x2-adjacent-to-x1 version of the A/D adjacency claim.

The E bloc parses the form as rusy-bavla-m-dei, not rusy-bavlam-dei. Head mdei ~ djedi is kept, but the modifier is rusy bavla ‘Russian language’. bavla is language, not balvi adjacency, and the lam material is read as the contact/offset linking rafsi of a day-measure family. On the usual djedi-derived measure lujvo place inheritance the modifier maps onto x1 only:
x1 = the interval/item being dated/measured, here a Russian-language day/interval,
x2 = the quantified offset expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1,
x3 = the day standard/calendar against which the count is made.
That is option E: x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’.

A/D readings, x2 adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, are the surface expression of the bavla/lamji adjacency component when the head is taken as medju/lamji rather than djedi. That misplaces the djedi standard place.

Current round 1 distribution is ~11 for G, 9 for E, with the E bloc now explicitly citing rusy = Russian fu’ivla, bavla = language, and the transparent segmentation rusy-bavla-m-dei. The G bloc retains the colour-rafsi reading for rusy- and the attested bavlamdei next-day place frame, giving the familiar x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard.

Unresolved: the actual rafsi inventory for rusku ‘gray’ vs rusko ‘Russian’ and whether bavlam- is a lexicalised next-to rafsi balvi/lamji or the concatenation bavla + lam. The head is unequivocally the day material mdei/dei; the dispute is whether the left material is a colour-modified adjacency modifier or a Russian-language measure modifier. The measure reading E resolves the morphology without forcing rusy = gray and keeps all three morphemes rusy-, bavla-, mdei- in their standard values; the colour-adjacency reading G keeps the classic next-day place inheritance but requires a non-standard use of rusy- for gray and a balvi reading for bavlam-.

I am retaining both analyses in memory with the shift in weight toward the rusy = Russian, bavla = language, mdei measure parsing that yields E, while noting the persistent G bloc’s place-structure argument and the adjacency A/D variant.
reflection_text.19:
The form is being debated as a right-headed tanru/lujvo with the day rafsi -mdei/-dei ~ djedi as the rightmost head. The dispute is essentially three-way, with the decisive split being the rafsi identity of rusy- and the segmentation of the middle material.

rusy- / rusy bavla:  
* G camp keeps rusy- as the rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’, a colour/metaphorical modifier of the head.  bavlam- is read as the balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’ material, so bavlamdei is the established next-day/adjacent-day lujvo.  
* E camp reads the string as rusy-bavla-m-dei.  rusy is the fu’ivla for Russian, bavla is ‘language/speech’, so rusy bavla = ‘Russian language’.  The colour rafsi would be rusku/rus-, not the fu’ivla rusy.  bavla is language, not balvi, and balvi’s rafsi is balvi-, not bavla-.

Place inheritance in the G / gray-adjacent-day analysis:
* Head = djedi-derived next-day selbri bavlamdei.  
  d1 = the day in question, d2 = the day that d1 is next to / precedes / follows, d3 = day standard / calendar.  
* rusy bavlam maps onto d1, so r1 = d1 is coloured gray / gray-adjacent.  
* r2 = d2 = the day that stands immediately next to / precedes the gray x1 day, r3 = d3 = day standard.  
This is the G description: x2 is the day preceding/adjacent to x1 and x3 is the ‘day standard’.  Colleagues 1,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 argue this is the classic right-head tanru mapping and that the rusy modifier only restricts x1.

Place inheritance in the E / Russian-language day-measure analysis:
* Head = mdei ~ djedi used as a day-count/measure head, modifier = rusy bavla ‘Russian language’.
* The head retains the djedi-derived measure places: x1 = the interval/item being dated/measured, x2 = the quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1, x3 = day standard / calendar against which the count is made.  
* rusy bavla only narrows x1 to a Russian-language reference; it does not create colour or adjacency places for x2/x3.  
Thus x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 = ‘day standard’.  Colleagues 10,13,14,16,17,2,21,5,7,9 favour this on the grounds that rusy bavla is a lexicalised language compound and bavla ≠ balvi, preserving all three morphemes.

A/D adjacency-of-x2-x3 reading:
* Treats the head as the adjacency/between relation medju/lamji so the two non-head places are the adjacency pair.  That yields x2 is adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3, with x3 as a property/sequence.  Colleagues 11,15,3,4,6,8 note this is essentially the same relation expressed without the day head, and it is subsumed by the G predecessor-day reading when the day head is kept.

Unresolved points carried forward:
* Exact rafsi identity of rusy: colour rafsi of rusku vs fu’ivla rusy ‘Russian’.  Both lines cite Lojban rafsi practice.
* Segmentation of the middle: rusy-bavlam-dei with bavlam = balvi+lamji next-to, vs rusy-bavla-m-dei with bavla = language + lam measure.
* Whether bavlamdei is an attested next-day lujvo with preserved d2 = preceding day, or a language-day measure construction.
* x3 is consistently day standard/calendar across G and E; the disagreement is x2: preceding/adjacent day vs number of full days.

Current belief remains split. The G analysis matches the standard right-head place inheritance and the documented bavlamdei ‘adjacent/next day’ frame, giving x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard. The E analysis matches the transparent rusy bavla ‘Russian language’ segmentation and the djedi-derived measure place pattern, giving x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 = day standard. The A/D adjacency pair is a re-phrasing of the bavlam relation; it does not change the x3 = standard consensus.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m coming around to the E reading, rusy-bavla-m-dei, and I think the rafsi inventory makes it quite strong.

reflection_text.1:
The segmentation debate is now heavily weighted to the measure reading but the gray-adjacent camp is not gone.

The split from round 1 was rusy = rusku ‘gray’ + bavlam = balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside’ giving a bavlamdei ‘adjacent/next day’ head with rusy colouring x1, i.e. G/x2 = day preceding x1, x3 = day standard, essentially the A/D adjacency instantiation. The alternative was rusy = Russian fu’ivla + bavla = ‘language’ + mdei = djedi ‘day’ giving rusy-bavla-m-dei ‘Russian-language day’ with a djedi-derived day-measure frame, i.e. E/x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1, x3 = day standard.

Round 2 public moves: the E bloc has grown markedly. Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14,15,16,17,19,2,20,21,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 now argue E. Colleague 10 switched from G to E this round; Colleague 1,11,13,14,15,16,17 also switched to E. Key arguments for E:

* Head-final on mdei ~ dei < djedi ‘day’. Left material is rusy bavla, not rusy bavlam.
* rusy is the conventional fu’ivla/rafsi for rusycu ‘Russian’. The colour gray is rusku, whose productive rafsi is rus-/rusku-, not the fu’ivla rusy.
* bavla is ‘language/speech’. balvi ‘be next to/be beside’ has rafsi balvi-/bal-, not bavla-. The -m- in the surface form is the regular linker bavla-m-dei, not a lexicalised bavlam- adjacency rafsi.
* With rusy bavla as x1 modifier of a mdei measure head, the head keeps its djedi-derived measure places: x1 = interval/item being dated/measured, x2 = quantity expressed in whole days corresponding to x1, x3 = day standard/calendar. rusy bavla only narrows x1 to Russian-language.

The G bloc now consists essentially of Colleagues 12 and 18, with earlier A/D support largely subsumed. Their arguments:

* bavlamdei is the regular balvi/lamji + djedi ‘adjacent/next day’ lujvo with frame d1 = day in question, d2 = day next to/preceding d1, d3 = day standard.
* rusy- is taken as the colour/metaphorical rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’ mapping onto d1 only, preserving r2 = preceding/adjacent day, r3 = day standard. This is the G description, an instantiation of the generic x2 adjacent to x3 reading A/D.
* They maintain tanru mapping: [(rusy bavlam) dei] with rusy colouring x1 only.

Unresolved points that remain important:

* Lexical status of rusy: fu’ivla for Russian vs colour rafsi of rusku. Both sides cite rafsi inventory.
* Whether bavla can be read as balvi adjacency or must be retained as ‘language’. E requires the transparent rusy-bavla-m-dei parse preserving all three morphemes; G requires reading bavla as adjacency and losing the language morpheme.
* Place merging: both camps agree x3 = ‘day standard’ is preserved; divergence is nature of x2: predecessor adjacent day vs numerical day count.
* The shared observation that A/D adjacency readings have largely been folded into G in round 1, and are now being displaced by E.

My current understanding: morphologically transparent rusy-bavla-m-dei with rusy = Russian, bavla = language, mdei = day measure is rafsi-consistent and preserves all morphemes, and is now the majority position in round 2. The gray-adjacent reading requires non-standard rafsi identifications for rusy and for bavla and is increasingly seen as a folk etymology that loses bavla ‘language’. The unresolved tension remains the attested status of bavlamdei as an adjacency lujvo versus the linker analysis bavla-m-dei.
reflection_text.10:
The form is head-final on mdei/dei ≃ djedi ‘day’. The decisive dispute is segmentation and rafsi inventory.

E / rusy-bavla-m-dei camp:
* rusy is the established fu’ivla/rafsi for Russian / rusycu, not the colour rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’ whose productive rafsi is rus-/rusku-, not rusy-.
* bavla = language/speech. balvi ‘be next to/be beside’ has rafsi balvi-, not bavla-.
* The transparent parse is rusy-bavla-m-dei = [rusy bavla] ‘Russian language’ modifying mdei ‘day’. The m in bavlam is the regular linker bavla-m-dei, not a lexicalised bavlam- ≃ balvi/lamji adjacency.
* With a djedi-derived measure head the inherited frame is x1 = interval/item being dated/measured, x2 = quantity expressed in whole days corresponding to x1 under chosen reckoning, x3 = day standard/calendar.
* rusy bavla maps onto x1 only, narrowing x1 to a Russian-language day/interval. It does not create colour or adjacency places for x2/x3. Hence x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’. This preserves all three morphemes: rusy = Russian, bavla = language, mdei = day.

G / rusy-bavlam-dei camp:
* Parse as rusy-bavlam-dei = rusy ‘gray’ / rusku modifying bavlamdei ‘next/adjacent day’.
* bavlam- = balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’ + djedi ‘day’.
* Tanru rule: rightmost selbri is head, left selbri maps onto head’s x1. djedi-based next-day frame: x1 = day in question, x2 = day next to/preceding x1, x3 = day standard/calendar.
* rusy colours x1 gray/metaphorically gray. Hence x2 = adjacent/preceding day of the gray x1, x3 = day standard. This is G, the day-specific instantiation of generic adjacency A/D.

Disagreement centres:
* rusy = rusku ‘gray’ vs rusy = Russian fu’ivla; rafsi inventory for gray vs Russian.
* bavlam- = balvi/lamji adjacency vs bavla ‘language’ + lam measure linker.
* Whether head’s frame is next-day predecessor x2/x3 standard G or measure count x2/x3 standard E.
Directionality of x2 relative to x1 is secondary.

Round 2 shift: majority now moves to E on rafsi grounds. Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14,15,16,17,19,2,20,21,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 argue the rusy-bavla-m-dei segmentation respects attested rafsi and keeps bavla ‘language’ in the parse. Minority G persists: colleagues 12,18 retain rusy as colour rafsi and bavlamdei as attested next-day lujvo with x2 = predecessor day, x3 = standard.

Unresolved: exact attestation of bavlamdei as lexicalised next-day lujvo and whether rusy- can be used as a colour rafsi in this context. My prior lean was G with rusy = gray modifying bavlamdei. Rafsi inventory evidence for rusy = Russian and bavla = language now weighs strongly toward E, while G remains coherent if rusy is read as colour and bavla as adjacency. Current weight is shifting toward E: x2 is number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 is ‘day standard’.
reflection_text.11:
The form is head-final on the day material mdei ~ dei ≃ djedi ‘day’. The critical split is between a left-branching colour-adjacent next-day reading and the measure reading.

The G / A / D bloc parses ((rusy bavlam) dei) with bavlamdei as balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’ + djedi. On that djedi-derived next-day frame
d1 = day in question, d2 = day that stands next to / precedes / follows d1, d3 = day standard/calendar.
rusy is taken as rusku ‘gray/grey’ rafsi and the modifier maps onto d1, giving
r1 = gray day, r2 = the day preceding / adjacent to r1, r3 = day standard.
That is the G description, essentially the A/D adjacency reading made explicit in the day place structure: x2 is the day preceding/adjacent to x1 and x3 is the day standard. The suppressed r4 of the bavlam modifier is merged in normal tanru mapping.

The E bloc now dominates round 2. The transparent segmentation is rusy-bavla-m-dei = [rusy bavla] mdei.
Morphological evidence repeatedly stressed:
* rusy is the fu’ivla/rafsi for rusycu ‘Russian’, not a colour rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’. The colour rafsi is rus-/rusku-, not rusy-.
* bavla = ‘language/speech’. balvi ‘be next to’ is not bavla; adjacency rafsi is balvi-/bal-, not bavla-.
* bavlam is bavla-m, the regular linker before dei, not a lexicalised bavlam ‘be adjacent’. So bavla-m-dei = bavla mdei ‘language-day’.
rusy bavla is the regular tanru ‘Russian language’ mapped onto x1 of the head. The modifier only narrows x1, it does not create colour or adjacency places for x2/x3.

With a djedi-derived measure head the inherited temporal-measure frame is preserved:
x1 = interval/item being dated/measured, here narrowed to a Russian-language day/interval,
x2 = quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1 under the chosen reckoning,
x3 = day standard/calendar against which the count is made.
Hence x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1 and x3 = ‘day standard’, the E reading.

The shared x3 = day standard is common to both camps; the difference is x2: predecessor/adjacent day in G vs numerical day count in E. The rafsi inventory and the need to keep all three morphemes rusy = Russian, bavla = language, mdei = day strongly favours E. G remains coherent only if rusy is allowed as a colour rafsi of rusku and bavlamdei is taken as an attested balvi/lamji + djedi next-day lujvo, which forces bavla to be read as adjacency and loses the language component.

Current best estimate after round 2 is E, with G as the morphologically strained alternative and A/D as the generic adjacency formulation of G. Unresolved tension is the exact status of rusy- as colour vs language marker and whether bavlam- can be read as balvi/lamji; the weight of public evidence now points to the language measure parse.
reflection_text.19:

x1 = the interval/item being dated/measured, here narrowed to a Russian-language day/interval

The shared point across camps is x3 = day standard; x2 remains the contested quantity vs predecessor day. Unresolved is whether any attested bavlamdei next-day lujvo with balvi material exists that could support G; current weight of rafsi evidence favors E.

reflection_text.12:
The deliberation has now moved decisively toward the Russian-language day-measure reading E, with only two holdouts for the gray-adjacent-day reading G.

Consensus E position, now held by colleagues 1,10,11,13,14,15,16,17,19,2,20,21,3,4,5,6,7,8,9:
* Morphology is head-final on mdei ~ dei < djedi ‘day’. Transparent segmentation is rusy-bavla-m-dei = [rusy bavla] mdei, not rusy-bavlam-dei.
* rusy is the fu’ivla/rafsi for rusycu ‘Russian’. The colour grey/gray is rusku with productive rafsi rus-/rusku-, not the fu’ivla rusy.
* bavla = ‘language/speech’. rusy bavla = the regular tanru ‘Russian language’. bavla is not balvi ‘be next to’; adjacency rafsi is balvi-, not bavla-. The -m- in bavlamdei is the regular linker bavla-m-dei, not a lexicalised bavlam- ‘adjacent’ morpheme.
* The left tanru maps onto x1 of the head only. The head is a djedi-derived measure/offset lujvo.
* Inherited djedi measure frame: x1 = interval/item being dated/measured, here narrowed to a Russian-language day/interval; x2 = quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1 under the chosen reckoning; x3 = day standard/calendar against which the count is made.
* Hence x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’. The rusy bavla modifier only qualifies x1, it does not create colour or adjacency places.

Remaining G position, colleagues 12 and 18:
* rusy- = rafsi of rusku ‘gray/grey’, a colour/metaphorical modifier of x1.
* bavlam- = balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’ + djedi, i.e. the attested bavlamdei ‘next-day/adjacent-day’ lujvo.
* Head-final tanru ((rusy bavlam) dei): modifier maps onto d1 of the head. Place frame from bavlamdei: d1 = day in question, d2 = day next to/precedes/follows d1, d3 = day standard.
* With rusy colouring x1, free places are x2 = day that stands immediately next to/precedes the gray x1 day, x3 = day standard. This is the G description, essentially the adjacency reading A/D.

Core rafsi ambiguity that drove the split is now largely settled in practice:
* rusy = Russian fu’ivla vs rusy- = rusku grey rafsi.
* bavla = language vs balvi/lamji adjacency.
* Whether bavlamdei is an established next-day lujvo with x2 = predecessor day, or bavla-m-dei is a language-day measure lujvo with x2 = day count.

Evidence repeatedly cited for E: rafsi inventory consistency, preservation of all three morphemes rusy = Russian, bavla = language, mdei = day, and the standard mdei measure x2/x3 mapping. No independent attestation of bavlam- adjacency rafsi; bavla-m linker is regular.

Evidence cited for G: traditional tanru place inheritance, head-final mapping onto d1, and the classic next-day place structure with x2 = adjacent/preceding day, x3 = standard. Shared x3 = day standard is common to both camps; the dispute is x2.

Changes in beliefs: earlier A/D adjacency camp largely converged onto G then switched to E; colleague 10 switched G→E in round 2 and now holds. Colleagues 1,11,15,19,20,3,4,6,8 moved from G/A/D to E in this round.

Unresolved: the precise historical attestation of bavlamdei as a lexicalised next-day lujvo vs the analytic bavla m dei measure formation. If bavlamdei were lexicalised, the G parse would be plausible, but the rafsi inventory argument strongly favours E.

My current understanding aligns with the large E consensus: the most likely interpretation of the second and third arguments is x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’.
reflection_text.18:
The segmentation is now the decisive issue.

The form is head-final on mdei/dei < djedi ‘day’. The dispute is between

* rusy-bavlam-dei = [(rusy bavlam) dei] with head = djedi next/adjacent-day
* rusy-bavla-m-dei = [rusy bavla] mdei with head = djedi measure

G / A/D camp: rusy- = rusku ‘gray/grey’ rafsi, bavlam- = balvi/lamji ‘be next to / be beside / be in contact with’. bavlamdei is the regular adjacent/next-day lujvo. In a right-headed tanru rusy bavlam maps onto x1 of the head only. djedi-derived next-day frame is
d1 = day in question
d2 = day that d1 stands next to / precedes / follows
d3 = day standard / calendar
Hence with rusy colouring x1:
x1 = gray day
x2 = day preceding/adjacent to x1
x3 = day standard
This is the G description, essentially the generic x2 adjacent/beside/next to/in contact with x3 reading A/D. The shared x3 = day standard is kept.

E camp, now majority in round 2: rusy = fu’ivla rafsi for rusycu ‘Russian’, bavla = ‘language/speech’, m = linker, dei = djedi ‘day’. Transparent segmentation is rusy-bavla-m-dei, i.e. [rusy bavla] ‘Russian language’ modifying a day-measure head. rusy is not the rusku colour rafsi; colour gray is rusku with rafsi rus-/rusku-, not rusy. bavla is language, not balvi ‘be next to’; adjacency rafsi is balvi-, not bavla-. With mdei as a djedi-derived measure head the inherited temporal-measure places are preserved and the modifier maps onto x1 only:
x1 = interval/item being dated/measured, here narrowed to Russian-language day/interval
x2 = quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1 under the chosen reckoning
x3 = day standard/calendar against which the count is made
x2 = number of full days corresponding to x1; x3 = ‘day standard’.

Evidence for E: rafsi inventory rusy = Russian fu’ivla, bavla = language, bavla-m-dei is the regular language-day measure formation, the linker m is present, all three morphemes are preserved, and the measure places are the standard mdei inheritance. Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14,15,16,17,19,2,20,21,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 argue for this.

Evidence for G: left-branching tanru rusy + bavlamdei with head djedi, rusy- as colour rafsi restricting x1, bavlam- as attested next-day material. Place inheritance keeps d2 = preceding day, d3 = standard. Colleagues 12,18 retain this; colleagues 10/11/12 earlier also argued G/A.

* Exact rafsi status of rusy for rusku vs rusko/Russian fu’ivla.
* Whether bavlamdei is a lexicalized next-day lujvo at all, or whether the surface bavlam is always bavla-m.
* Directionality of x2 under G: preceding vs following, and whether the generic A/D x2 adjacent to x3 reading is a re-description of the same x1–x2 adjacency.

Belief update: Round 1 best synthesis was G with E as strong alternative. Round 2 public push heavily favors the rafsi-consistent rusy-bavla-m-dei segmentation and the djedi measure frame E. G remains morphologically coherent if rusy is read as colour and bavlam as adjacency, but it requires re-identifying bavla as balvi and rusy as a colour rafsi against the established inventory. Current best reading is therefore E: x2 is the number of full days corresponding to x1 and x3 is the day standard, with G as the main dissenting alternative.

The current weight of the morphological evidence is for the transparent head-final parse

*rusy-bavla-m-dei* = [rusy bavla] mdei

with mdei ~ dei < djedi ‘day’ as the head.

* rusy- is the fu’ivla/rafsi conventionally used for rusycu ‘Russian’. The grey/gray gismu is rusku and its productive colour rafsi is rus-/rusku-, not the fu’ivla rusy-.
* bavla is ‘language/speech’. balvi ‘be next to/be beside’ has rafsi balvi-/bal-, not bavla-. The surface -bavlam- is bavla-m-, the regular linker between bavla and dei, not an independent *bavlam- ‘be adjacent’ rafsi.

Hence rusy bavla is the regular tanru ‘Russian language’. In a right-headed tanru the left material maps onto x1 of the head only and does not create new colour or adjacency places.

With a djedi-derived measure head the inherited temporal-measure frame is preserved:

x1 = the interval/item being dated / measured,
x2 = the quantity expressed in whole days that corresponds to x1 under the chosen reckoning,
x3 = the day standard / calendar against which the count is made.

rusy bavla only narrows the kind of x1 – a Russian-language day / Russian-language dated interval – it does not turn bavla into balvi/lamji adjacency and it does not make rusy a colour modifier.

The G / A/D next-day reading would require the segmentation ((rusy bavlam) dei) with rusy- = rusku ‘gray’ and bavlam- = balvi/lamji ‘be next to’. That forces bavla to be read as adjacency and loses the bavla ‘language’ morpheme that is actually present, and it uses rusy- as a colour rafsi contrary to the established rafsi inventory.

The rafsi-consistent parse therefore keeps the mdei measure places free:

x2 is the number of full days corresponding to x1
x3 is the ‘day standard’

which is E.
